Subject: Analytic subprocessor edge-routing carveout / SCCs & UK Addendum question

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and privacy teams:

1) Our platform ingests EU personal data and we use a third-party analytics vendor (AnalyticsX) that insists on hitting an EU-edge collector before processing. They want a carveout in the DPA that requires EU-only routing for that subprocessor. Can Redwood accept a routing carveout that will be (a) limited to named analytics subprocessors, (b) covered by SCCs + UK Addendum, and (c) scoped via a Supplemental TIA (DTIA) for the analytics flows only?

2) If a carveout is possible, we will need evidence: certified subprocessor list with residency, confirmation of audit logs for routing, and a timeline for implementing the EU-edge routing fallback.

We'd like to understand operational impact and any SLA/price implications.

I've attached the redline our counsel proposed (attachment: medanalytics_dpa_redline_v2.pdf). Happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Alex Perez
Senior Counsel, MedAnalytics
alex.perez@medanalytics.com
(attachment: medanalytics_dpa_redline_v2.pdf (pdf))

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Perez <alex.perez@medanalytics.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Analytic subprocessor edge-routing carveout / SCCs & UK Addendum question

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. High level answer: we can support a narrowly-scoped routing carveout for named analytics subprocessors, but it requires two compensating controls and a small operational change:

- Controls required:
  * Pseudonymization at ingestion for EU-origin data before it leaves EU-edge collectors (to limit residual personal data exposure).
  * Enhanced audit logging (per-request routing tags + preserved KV audit entries) retained for 12 months and available for customer review.

- Operational change:
  * We'll bind a per-account routing policy to pin requests for the named subprocessor to EU-edge collectors. This will add an occasional cold-cache latency for those flows and requires a brief provisioning window (2–4 business days) to enable.

I attached a Redwood-redlined DPA (attachment: redline_DPA_KP_v3.pdf) and a simple diagram of the proposed edge-routing (attachment: edge_routing_diagram.png). Key legal notes in the redline: we accept SCCs + UK Addendum but need the Supplemental TIA to be scoped and time-limited to the analytics pipeline only; blanket carveouts are not acceptable.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the named analytics subprocessors and their residency assertions.
2) We run an operational impact assessment (2 business days) — I'll loop David for that.
3) Assuming ops feasibility, Laura will approve the limited TIA approach and we can circulate a DocuSign for the redline.

If you want to talk through the technical bit, I can be available tomorrow 10–11am GMT.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
(attachment: redline_DPA_KP_v3.pdf (pdf); attachment: edge_routing_diagram.png (png))

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Perez <alex.perez@medanalytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Analytic subprocessor edge-routing carveout / SCCs & UK Addendum question

Kimberly / Alex —

Operational notes from infra:

- Feasibility: We already support regional routing policies per-customer. Pinning named subprocessors to EU-edge collectors is straightforward if the subprocessor's ingress hostname/IPs are known.

- Latency/cost: Expect a small increase in p50 for those routed requests (typical +12–30ms) due to on-edge preprocessing; token-cost unchanged. If AnalyticsX requires a dedicated onshore cache/fallback we may need a reserved capacity slot (pricing TBD).

- Implementation steps (estimate):
  1) Add routing policy and update customer config (1 day).
  2) QA on dev cluster and run a sample traffic validation (1 day).
  3) Enable in prod (0.5 day) — total: 2–3 business days from go-ahead.

- Evidence we can provide by default: subprocessor invocation logs (time, target edge, request id), and exported routing policy snapshot. For stronger proof we can provide a signed attestation and a one-off CSV of routing events (subject to data minimization).

Open questions:
- Do we need to pseudonymize within the edge collector (before forwarding) or is a hashed identifier sufficient? Hashing has trade-offs for re-identification risks.

Happy to run the impact assessment once Alex confirms the AnalyticsX hostnames and residency.

—David
David Kim
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
(attachment: none)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Analytic subprocessor edge-routing carveout / SCCs & UK Addendum question

Alex —

Thanks. From a leadership perspective I'm comfortable approving a time-limited, narrowly scoped routing carveout conditioned on:

- Named subprocessors only (list to be finalized).
- Supplemental TIA limited to analytics pipeline and expires in 12 months unless renewed.
- 12-month audit log retention and a one-time attestation delivered within 14 days of go-live.
- A fallback clause: if routing causes service degradation beyond agreed SLOs, Redwood may route the traffic to the next compatible region while notifying MedAnalytics and working on remediation.

If that aligns with your legal team's needs, Kimberly please send the DocuSign link when ready and David will schedule the impact assessment.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
